claim: Using deep mutational scanning, yeast were engineered with all 44,604 single codon changes encoding 14,160 amino acid variants in Hsp90.
source: Using deep mutational scanning, we engineered yeast with all 44,604 single codon changes encoding 14,160 amino acid variants in Hsp90 and quantified growth effects under standard conditions and under five stress conditions.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the number of codon changes and amino acid variants engineered in the study.

claim: Growth effects of Hsp90 variants were quantified under standard conditions and under five stress conditions.
source: Using deep mutational scanning, we engineered yeast with all 44,604 single codon changes encoding 14,160 amino acid variants in Hsp90 and quantified growth effects under standard conditions and under five stress conditions.
evidence: The abstract describes the experimental design of measuring growth effects under multiple conditions.

claim: These are the largest determined comprehensive fitness maps of point mutants.
source: To our knowledge, these are the largest determined comprehensive fitness maps of point mutants.
evidence: The authors explicitly state this is the largest such study to their knowledge.

claim: The growth of many Hsp90 variants differed between conditions.
source: The growth of many variants differed between conditions, indicating that environment can have a large impact on Hsp90 evolution.
evidence: The abstract states that many variants showed different growth between conditions.

claim: Environment can have a large impact on Hsp90 evolution.
source: The growth of many variants differed between conditions, indicating that environment can have a large impact on Hsp90 evolution.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed data on variant growth differences.

claim: Multiple Hsp90 variants provided growth advantages under individual conditions.
source: Multiple variants provided growth advantages under individual conditions; however, these variants tended to exhibit growth defects in other environments.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that multiple variants were beneficial in specific conditions.

claim: Variants that provided growth advantages under individual conditions tended to exhibit growth defects in other environments.
source: Multiple variants provided growth advantages under individual conditions; however, these variants tended to exhibit growth defects in other environments.
evidence: The abstract describes a trade-off pattern observed in the data.

claim: The diversity of Hsp90 sequences observed in extant eukaryotes preferentially contains variants that supported robust growth under all tested conditions.
source: The diversity of Hsp90 sequences observed in extant eukaryotes preferentially contains variants that supported robust growth under all tested conditions.
evidence: The abstract states this finding from comparing natural variants to experimental fitness data.

claim: The long-term selective pressure on Hsp90 may have been that of fluctuating environments, leading to robustness under a variety of conditions.
source: Rather than favoring substitutions in individual conditions, the long-term selective pressure on Hsp90 may have been that of fluctuating environments, leading to robustness under a variety of conditions.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on their findings.

claim: Environmental conditions can alter the fitness effects of mutations.
source: It has long been clear that environmental conditions can alter the fitness effects of mutations (Tutt, 1896).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a historical citation.

claim: Mutations can be categorized into three classes: strongly deleterious mutations, nearly-neutral mutations, and beneficial mutations.
source: Depending on environmental conditions, mutations can be categorized into three classes: strongly deleterious mutations that are purged from populations by purifying selection, nearly-neutral mutations that are governed by stochastic processes, and beneficial mutations that tend to provide a selective advantage (Ohta, 1973).
evidence: This classification is cited from Ohta, 1973.

claim: The EMPIRIC approach quantifies growth rates that are a direct measure of experimental fitness.
source: The EMPIRIC (Exceedingly Meticulous and Parallel Investigation of Randomized Individual Codons) approach that we previously developed (Hietpas et al., 2011) is particularly well suited to address questions regarding the environmental impact of mutational effects for three reasons: it quantifies growth rates that are a direct measure of experimental fitness, all point mutations are engineered providing comprehensive maps of growth effects, and all the variants can be tracked in the same flask while experiencing identical growth conditions.
evidence: The authors describe the capabilities of their method.

claim: The EMPIRIC approach engineers all point mutations providing comprehensive maps of growth effects.
source: The EMPIRIC (Exceedingly Meticulous and Parallel Investigation of Randomized Individual Codons) approach that we previously developed (Hietpas et al., 2011) is particularly well suited to address questions regarding the environmental impact of mutational effects for three reasons: it quantifies growth rates that are a direct measure of experimental fitness, all point mutations are engineered providing comprehensive maps of growth effects, and all the variants can be tracked in the same flask while experiencing identical growth conditions.
evidence: The authors describe the capabilities of their method.

claim: In the EMPIRIC approach, all variants can be tracked in the same flask while experiencing identical growth conditions.
source: The EMPIRIC (Exceedingly Meticulous and Parallel Investigation of Randomized Individual Codons) approach that we previously developed (Hietpas et al., 2011) is particularly well suited to address questions regarding the environmental impact of mutational effects for three reasons: it quantifies growth rates that are a direct measure of experimental fitness, all point mutations are engineered providing comprehensive maps of growth effects, and all the variants can be tracked in the same flask while experiencing identical growth conditions.
evidence: The authors describe the capabilities of their method.

claim: Stress environments can exacerbate the fitness defects of mutations in ubiquitin.
source: The analysis of ubiquitin fitness maps revealed that stress environments can exacerbate the fitness defects of mutations.
evidence: This is a finding from previous work on ubiquitin cited by the authors.

claim: There are only three amino acid differences in ubiquitin between yeast and human.
source: However, the small size of ubiquitin and the near absence of natural variation in ubiquitin sequences (only three amino acid differences between yeast and human) hindered investigation of the properties underlying historically observed substitutions.
evidence: This is stated as a fact about ubiquitin sequence conservation.

claim: Hsp90 encodes a 709 amino acid protein.
source: Hsp90 encodes a 709 amino acid protein and to our knowledge it is the largest gene for which a comprehensive protein fitness map has been determined.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the size of Hsp90.

claim: Hsp90 is the largest gene for which a comprehensive protein fitness map has been determined.
source: Hsp90 encodes a 709 amino acid protein and to our knowledge it is the largest gene for which a comprehensive protein fitness map has been determined.
evidence: The authors state this is the largest such study to their knowledge.

claim: Hsp90 is an essential and highly abundant molecular chaperone.
source: Hsp90 is an essential and highly abundant molecular chaperone which is induced by a wide variety of environmental stresses (Gasch et al., 2000; Lindquist, 1981).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Hsp90 is induced by a wide variety of environmental stresses.
source: Hsp90 is an essential and highly abundant molecular chaperone which is induced by a wide variety of environmental stresses (Gasch et al., 2000; Lindquist, 1981).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Hsp90 assists cells in responding to stressful conditions by facilitating the folding and activation of client proteins through ATP-dependent conformational changes mediated by co-chaperones.
source: Hsp90 assists cells in responding to these stressful conditions by facilitating the folding and activation of client proteins through a series of ATP-dependent conformational changes mediated by co-chaperones (Krukenberg et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the known mechanism of Hsp90 function with a citation.

claim: Hsp90 clients are primarily signal transduction proteins, highly enriched in kinases and transcription factors.
source: These clients are primarily signal transduction proteins, highly enriched in kinases and transcription factors (Taipale et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Through its clients, Hsp90 activity is linked to virtually every cellular process.
source: Through its clients, Hsp90 activity is linked to virtually every cellular process.
evidence: This is an inference based on the broad range of Hsp90 clients.

claim: Hsp90 can facilitate the emergence and evolution of new traits in response to stress conditions, including drug resistance in fungi.
source: Hsp90 can facilitate the emergence and evolution of new traits in response to stress conditions, including drug resistance in fungi (Cowen and Lindquist, 2005), gross morphology in flies (Rutherford and Lindquist, 1998) and plants (Queitsch et al., 2002), and vision loss in cave fish (Rohner et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with multiple citations supporting different examples.

claim: Hsp90 can facilitate the emergence and evolution of new traits in response to stress conditions, including gross morphology in flies.
source: Hsp90 can facilitate the emergence and evolution of new traits in response to stress conditions, including drug resistance in fungi (Cowen and Lindquist, 2005), gross morphology in flies (Rutherford and Lindquist, 1998) and plants (Queitsch et al., 2002), and vision loss in cave fish (Rohner et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with multiple citations supporting different examples.

claim: Hsp90 can facilitate the emergence and evolution of new traits in response to stress conditions, including gross morphology in plants.
source: Hsp90 can facilitate the emergence and evolution of new traits in response to stress conditions, including drug resistance in fungi (Cowen and Lindquist, 2005), gross morphology in flies (Rutherford and Lindquist, 1998) and plants (Queitsch et al., 2002), and vision loss in cave fish (Rohner et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with multiple citations supporting different examples.

claim: Hsp90 can facilitate the emergence and evolution of new traits in response to stress conditions, including vision loss in cave fish.
source: Hsp90 can facilitate the emergence and evolution of new traits in response to stress conditions, including drug resistance in fungi (Cowen and Lindquist, 2005), gross morphology in flies (Rutherford and Lindquist, 1998) and plants (Queitsch et al., 2002), and vision loss in cave fish (Rohner et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with multiple citations supporting different examples.

claim: An abundance of Hsp90 promotes standing variation by masking the phenotypic effects of destabilizing mutations in clients in non-stress conditions.
source: In non-stress conditions, an abundance of Hsp90 promotes standing variation by masking the phenotypic effects of destabilizing mutations in clients.
evidence: This describes a known mechanism of Hsp90 function.

claim: Stressful conditions that tax Hsp90 capacity can manifest in phenotypic diversity that can contribute to adaptation.
source: Stressful conditions that tax Hsp90 capacity can then manifest in phenotypic diversity that can contribute to adaptation.
evidence: This describes a known mechanism of Hsp90 function.

claim: The sequence of Hsp90 is strongly conserved in eukaryotes with 57% amino acid identity from yeast to human.
source: However, the sequence of Hsp90 is strongly conserved in eukaryotes (57% amino acid identity from yeast to human), indicating consistent strong purifying selection.
evidence: This is a factual statement about Hsp90 sequence conservation.

claim: The strong conservation of Hsp90 sequence indicates consistent strong purifying selection.
source: However, the sequence of Hsp90 is strongly conserved in eukaryotes (57% amino acid identity from yeast to human), indicating consistent strong purifying selection.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed sequence conservation.

claim: 98% of possible amino acid changes in Hsp90 were quantified in bulk competitions.
source: Bulk competitions of yeast with a deep sequencing readout enabled the simultaneous quantification of 98% of possible amino acid changes (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the coverage achieved in the experimental approach.

claim: Selection coefficients between technical replicates under standard conditions were strongly correlated (R2 = 0.90).
source: Selection coefficients between replicates were strongly correlated (R2 = 0.90), and indicated that we could clearly distinguish between selection coefficients for members of the library containing silent mutations that do not change the amino acid sequence (wild-type synonyms) and those containing stop codons (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the reproducibility analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Selection coefficients in this study under standard conditions correlated strongly (R2 = 0.87) with estimates of the Hsp90 N-domain in a previous study.
source: The selection coefficients in this study under standard conditions also correlated strongly (R2 = 0.87) with estimates of the Hsp90 N-domain in a previous study (Mishra et al., 2016; Figure 1—figure supplement 2), indicating that biological replicates also show high reproducibility.
evidence: This compares current results to a previous study, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Most variants of Hsp90 had wild-type-like fitness in the competition experiment in standard conditions.
source: However, most variants of Hsp90 had wild-type-like fitness in the competition experiment in standard conditions (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a summary of the fitness distribution observed in standard conditions, shown in Figure 1C.

claim: All possible mutations (excluding stops) were compatible with function at 425 positions in Hsp90.
source: All possible mutations (excluding stops) were compatible with function at 425 positions.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the fitness data.

claim: Only 17 positions in Hsp90 had low mutational tolerance to the extent that 15 or more substitutions caused null-like growth defects.
source: Only 17 positions had low mutational tolerance to the extent that 15 or more substitutions caused null-like growth defects (R32, E33, N37, D40, D79, G81, G94, I96, A97, S99, G118, G121, G123, Y125, F156, W300, and R380).
evidence: This is a quantitative result identifying specific critical positions.

claim: All critical positions except W300 are in contact with ATP or mediate ATP-dependent conformational changes in the N-domain of Hsp90.
source: All these positions except for W300 are in contact with ATP or mediate ATP-dependent conformational changes in the N-domain of Hsp90.
evidence: This is a structural analysis of the critical positions identified.

claim: W300 transmits information from client binding to long range conformational changes of Hsp90 that are driven by ATP hydrolysis.
source: While W300 does not contact ATP, it transmits information from client binding to long range conformational changes of Hsp90 that are driven by ATP hydrolysis (Röhl et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to explain the functional role of W300.

claim: The average selection coefficient at different positions in standard growth conditions correlates (R2 = 0.49) with distance from ATP.
source: In fact, the average selection coefficient at different positions (a measure of mutational sensitivity) in standard growth conditions correlates (R2 = 0.49) with distance from ATP (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a quantitative correlation analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: ATP binding and the conformational changes driven by ATP hydrolysis impose dominant physical constraints in Hsp90 under standard laboratory conditions.
source: Our results indicate that ATP binding and the conformational changes driven by ATP hydrolysis impose dominant physical constraints in Hsp90 under standard laboratory conditions.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the correlation between fitness and distance from ATP.

claim: All tested stress conditions reduced the growth rate of the parental strain within a two-fold range.
source: Consistently, all stresses reduced the growth rate of the parental strain within a two-fold range, with depletion of nitrogen levels causing the smallest reduction in growth rate and diamide causing the greatest reduction (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from growth rate measurements shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Depletion of nitrogen levels caused the smallest reduction in growth rate among the tested stresses.
source: Consistently, all stresses reduced the growth rate of the parental strain within a two-fold range, with depletion of nitrogen levels causing the smallest reduction in growth rate and diamide causing the greatest reduction (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from growth rate measurements shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Diamide caused the greatest reduction in growth rate among the tested stresses.
source: Consistently, all stresses reduced the growth rate of the parental strain within a two-fold range, with depletion of nitrogen levels causing the smallest reduction in growth rate and diamide causing the greatest reduction (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from growth rate measurements shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Under standard conditions, the normal level of Hsp90 protein can be dramatically reduced without major impacts on growth rate.
source: Under standard conditions, the normal level of Hsp90 protein can be dramatically reduced without major impacts on growth rate, consistent with previous findings (Jiang et al., 2013; Picard et al., 1990).
evidence: This is stated as a finding consistent with previous studies.

claim: Reduced Hsp90 levels cause a marked decrease in growth rate at 37°C.
source: Consistent with this concept, reduced Hsp90 levels cause a marked decrease in growth rate at 37°C.
evidence: This is a result from the growth rate measurements at elevated temperature.

claim: The stresses of 37°C and diamide tend to exaggerate the growth defects of many mutants compared to standard conditions.
source: The stresses of 37°C and diamide tend to exaggerate the growth defects of many mutants compared to standard conditions, whereas high salt and ethanol tend to rescue growth defects (Figure 2B&C and Figure 2—figure supplement 9).
evidence: This is a summary of the comparative fitness data shown in Figure 2B&C.

claim: High salt and ethanol tend to rescue growth defects compared to standard conditions.
source: The stresses of 37°C and diamide tend to exaggerate the growth defects of many mutants compared to standard conditions, whereas high salt and ethanol tend to rescue growth defects (Figure 2B&C and Figure 2—figure supplement 9).
evidence: This is a summary of the comparative fitness data shown in Figure 2B&C.

claim: The average selection coefficients are more deleterious in diamide and temperature stress compared to standard conditions.
source: The average selection coefficients are more deleterious in diamide and temperature stress compared to standard conditions.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of fitness distributions across conditions.

claim: The average selection coefficients are less deleterious in ethanol and salt stress than in standard conditions.
source: In contrast, the average selection coefficients are less deleterious in ethanol and salt stress than in standard conditions, which suggests a decrease in the demand for Hsp90 function in these conditions.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of fitness distributions across conditions.

claim: Environmentally responsive positions with large changes in average selection coefficient in at least three conditions are located throughout all domains of Hsp90.
source: Unlike the critical positions that cluster around the ATP binding site (Figure 1C), the environmentally responsive positions are located throughout all domains of Hsp90.
evidence: This is a structural analysis of environmentally responsive positions.

claim: Environmentally responsive positions are more conserved in nature compared to other positions in Hsp90.
source: Similar to critical residues, environmentally responsive positions are more conserved in nature compared to other positions in Hsp90 (Figure 3C), suggesting that the suite of experimental stress conditions tested captured aspects of natural selection pressures on Hsp90 sequence.
evidence: This is a comparison of conservation patterns shown in Figure 3C.

claim: About 65% of the environmentally responsive residues have been identified as interacting with binding partners.
source: About 65% of the environmentally responsive residues have been identified either structurally or genetically as interacting with binding partners (Ali et al., 2006; Bohen and Yamamoto, 1993; Genest et al., 2013; Hagn et al., 2011; Hawle et al., 2006; Kravats et al., 2018; Lorenz et al., 2014; Meyer et al., 2003; Meyer et al., 2004; Nathan and Lindquist, 1995; Retzlaff et al., 2009; Roe et al., 2004; Verba et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2010), compared to about 15% of positions that were not responsive to stress conditions.
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of binding site enrichment with multiple citations.

claim: About 15% of positions that were not responsive to stress conditions have been identified as interacting with binding partners.
source: About 65% of the environmentally responsive residues have been identified either structurally or genetically as interacting with binding partners (Ali et al., 2006; Bohen and Yamamoto, 1993; Genest et al., 2013; Hagn et al., 2011; Hawle et al., 2006; Kravats et al., 2018; Lorenz et al., 2014; Meyer et al., 2003; Meyer et al., 2004; Nathan and Lindquist, 1995; Retzlaff et al., 2009; Roe et al., 2004; Verba et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2010), compared to about 15% of positions that were not responsive to stress conditions.
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of binding site enrichment with multiple citations.

claim: Client and co-chaperone interactions have a larger impact on experimental fitness under stress conditions compared to standard conditions.
source: While ATP binding and hydrolysis are the main structural determinants that constrain fitness in standard growth conditions, client and co-chaperone interactions have a larger impact on experimental fitness under stress conditions.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the enrichment of environmentally responsive positions at binding sites.

claim: Of the 2504 variants of Hsp90 that are deleterious when grown at 37°C, 884 of them (~35%) are deleterious only in this condition.
source: Of the 2504 variants of Hsp90 that are deleterious when grown at 37°C, 884 of them (~35%) are deleterious only in this condition (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 3F.

claim: 663 Hsp90 amino acid changes (roughly 5% of possible changes) were found to be temperature sensitive.
source: Based on this definition, 663 Hsp90 amino acid changes (roughly 5% of possible changes) were found to be temperature sensitive (Figure 4A, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result identifying temperature-sensitive mutations shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Temperature-sensitive mutations tended to concentrate at certain amino acid positions of Hsp90.
source: We found that ts mutations tended to concentrate at certain amino acid positions of Hsp90 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a result from the clustering analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The clustering of temperature-sensitive mutations was significant compared to random simulations.
source: The clustering of ts mutations was significant compared to random simulations.
evidence: This is a statistical result from comparing observed clustering to simulations.

claim: Substitutions that confer a temperature-sensitive phenotype are enriched in buried residues.
source: Consistent with the idea that many ts mutations may disrupt protein folding at elevated temperature, substitutions that confer a ts phenotype are enriched in buried residues (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a result from the SASA analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Temperature-sensitive mutations tend to have negative Blosum scores.
source: Also consistent with this idea, ts mutations tend to have negative Blosum scores (Henikoff and Henikoff, 1992; Figure 4E), a hallmark of disruptive amino acid changes.
evidence: This is a result from the Blosum score analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The I66E, G170D and L499R Hsp90 mutants have no activity at 37°C irrespective of expression levels.
source: The I66E, G170D and L499R Hsp90 mutants have no activity at 37°C irrespective of expression levels.
evidence: This is a result from testing individual mutants at different expression levels.

claim: Increasing the Hsp90 expression levels at least partially rescued the growth defect for five temperature-sensitive variants (L50D, K102A, D180L, K398L, K594I).
source: In contrast, increasing the Hsp90 expression levels at least partially rescued the growth defect for five ts variants (L50D, K102A, D180L, K398L, K594I), indicating that these variants do not provide enough Hsp90 function for robust growth at elevated temperature.
evidence: This is a result from testing individual mutants at different expression levels.

claim: The largest number of beneficial variants in Hsp90 occurred in high temperature and diamide conditions.
source: The largest number of beneficial variants in Hsp90 occurred in high temperature and diamide conditions (Figure 5A, Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Beneficial mutants in diamide and high temperature tend to cluster at specific positions.
source: Second, beneficial mutants in diamide and high temperature tend to cluster at certain positions (Figure 5B), which would not be expected for noise.
evidence: This is a result from the clustering analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: In diamide and elevated temperature, the clustered beneficial positions were almost entirely located in the ATP-binding domain and the middle domain.
source: In diamide and elevated temperature, the clustered beneficial positions were almost entirely located in the ATP-binding domain and the middle domain (Figure 5C), both of which make extensive contacts with clients and co-chaperones (Ali et al., 2006; Meyer et al., 2003; Meyer et al., 2004; Roe et al., 2004; Verba et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a structural analysis of beneficial positions shown in Figure 5C with citations.

claim: Beneficial mutations in elevated temperature and diamide conditions were preferentially located on the surface of Hsp90.
source: Beneficial mutations in elevated temperature and diamide conditions were preferentially located on the surface of Hsp90 (Figure 5D) at positions accessible to binding partners.
evidence: This is a result from the SASA analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Beneficial positions were disproportionately located at known interfaces with co-chaperones and clients.
source: Analyses of available Hsp90 complexes indicate that beneficial positions were disproportionately located at known interfaces with co-chaperones and clients (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a result from the interface analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Amino acids that are beneficial in diamide and elevated temperature tend to exhibit deleterious effects in standard conditions.
source: Amino acids that are beneficial in diamide and elevated temperature tend to exhibit deleterious effects in standard conditions (Figure 5F), consistent with a cost of adaptation.
evidence: This is a result from comparing fitness across conditions shown in Figure 5F.

claim: A synonymous mutation at the beginning of Hsp90 that was beneficial at high temperature was expressed at higher level in the plasmid system.
source: Analysis of an individual clone confirms that a synonymous mutation at the beginning of Hsp90 that was beneficial at high temperature was expressed at higher level in our plasmid system (Figure 5—figure supplement 4C,D).
evidence: This is a result from analyzing individual clones shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4C,D.

claim: 1750 amino acid differences in total were located at 499 positions in Hsp90 across 267 sequences from organisms that broadly span across eukaryotes.
source: We identified 1750 amino acid differences in total that were located at 499 positions in Hsp90.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the natural sequence analysis.

claim: The vast majority of natural amino acids in Hsp90 had wild-type-like fitness in all conditions studied.
source: The vast majority of natural amino acids had wild-type-like fitness in all conditions studied here (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This is a result from comparing natural variants to experimental fitness shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: Naturally occurring amino acids in Hsp90 were rarely deleterious in any experimental condition.
source: Whereas naturally occurring amino acids in Hsp90 were rarely deleterious in any experimental condition, they were similarly likely to provide a growth benefit compared to all possible amino acids (5%).
evidence: This is a result from comparing natural variants to experimental fitness.

claim: Naturally occurring amino acids in Hsp90 were similarly likely to provide a growth benefit compared to all possible amino acids (5%).
source: Whereas naturally occurring amino acids in Hsp90 were rarely deleterious in any experimental condition, they were similarly likely to provide a growth benefit compared to all possible amino acids (5%).
evidence: This is a result from comparing natural variants to experimental fitness.

claim: Condition-dependent fitness benefits are not a major determinant of natural variation in Hsp90 sequences.
source: This observation indicates that condition-dependent fitness benefits are not a major determinant of natural variation in Hsp90 sequences.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the finding that natural variants are not enriched for beneficial effects.

claim: Natural selection has favored Hsp90 substitutions that are robust to multiple stressful conditions.
source: Instead, our results indicate that natural selection has favored Hsp90 substitutions that are robust to multiple stressful conditions (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the finding that natural variants support robust growth across conditions.

claim: The clustering of beneficial mutations at known binding interfaces suggests that the optimal binding affinity for partner proteins may depend on growth conditions.
source: The clustering of beneficial mutations at known binding interfaces suggests that the optimal binding affinity for partner proteins may depend on growth conditions.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural location of beneficial mutations.

claim: Natural variants of Hsp90 have been selected for binding properties that are robust to different stresses rather than specific to individual conditions.
source: We propose that natural variants of Hsp90 have been selected for binding properties that are robust to different stresses rather than specific to individual conditions.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on their findings.
